issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares getTotalNumberOfStudents() as returning a String, but the solution implementation returns an int. The textual task asks students to check the UML for the expected return type, which would lead them to implement a String-returning method, while the provided solution (and typical numerical semantics) use an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the correct return type and cause failing tests or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across artifacts. Preferably update the UML and problem text to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (since it represents a numeric total), or alternatively change the solution to return a String if that was the intended design. Ensure the template method signature (when added) matches the chosen return type so students have a consistent specification to implement.
